claims.text: Changing the composition of HfMoTaTiZr according to a eutectic high-entropy-alloy design will produce a eutectic microstructure.
The proposed composition change will reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed composition change will preserve strong room-temperature and high-temperature mechanical performance.
The eutectic microstructure will refine the grain size.
The eutectic microstructure will reduce segregation.
The eutectic microstructure will optimize the phase distribution.
Grain refinement, reduced segregation, and optimized phase distribution will improve mechanical properties.
Grain refinement, reduced segregation, and optimized phase distribution will reduce density.
Density will decrease by at least 5% relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Room-temperature yield strength will remain above 1500 MPa.
Yield strength at 1000 °C will remain above 800 MPa.
The magnitude of density reduction and mechanical-property retention will depend on the specific composition.
The magnitude of density reduction and mechanical-property retention will depend on processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 5% density reduction, but the rejection rule rejects only reductions below 3%. A result between 3% and 5% would violate the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.

The prediction requires strengths above 1500 MPa at room temperature and 800 MPa at 1000 °C, whereas the rejection rule permits losses of up to 10% from the stated approximate baselines of 1600 and 855 MPa, corresponding to approximately 1440 and 770 MPa. Thus some outcomes below the predicted minimum strengths would not trigger rejection.
